news.title: 【SMM Analysis】Philippines & Indonesia Nickel Ore Prices Weaken as Rainy-Season Supply Tightens and HPM FallsPhilippines: Nickel Ore Prices Continue to Decline as Rainy-Season Supply Tightness Fails to Offset Weak Demand On the pricing front, Philippine nickel ore prices continued to decline across all grades this week, extending the market’s bearish trend. For low-grade ore, 0.7% Ni, Al ≥5% fell to US$16–17/t, with a midpoint of US$16.5/t, down US$1/t from the previous period. 0.7% Ni, Al <5% declined to US$22–24/t, with a midpoint of US$23/t, also down US$1/t. 0.9% Ni, Al 7% min dropped to US$15–17/wmt, with a midpoint of US$16/wmt, down US$1/wmt, while 0.9% Ni, Al 7% max declined to US$22–23/wmt, with a midpoint of US$22.5/wmt, likewise down US$1/wmt. The decline was more pronounced for medium- to high-grade ore. 1.3% Ni fell to US$27–29/wmt, with a midpoint of US$28/wmt; 1.4% Ni declined to US$37–39/wmt, with a midpoint of US$38/wmt; 1.5% Ni dropped to US$44–47/wmt, with a midpoint of US$45.5/wmt; and 1.8% Ni fell to US$72–74/wmt, with a midpoint of US$73/wmt. All of these grades were down US$2/wmt from the previous period. The continued weakness in Philippine nickel ore prices is mainly driven by cautious downstream procurement and broader pressure across the regional nickel ore market. Downstream raw material inventories in China remain relatively ample and are estimated to be sufficient for around two months. Spot purchases are therefore largely limited to essential restocking needs. With no significant increase in demand, buyers have shown limited willingness to accept higher-priced imported ore, placing continued downward pressure on quotations from Philippine mines. At the same time, freight rates from the Philippines to China remain relatively high, meaning reductions in FOB prices have not fully translated into a stronger purchasing advantage on a CIF basis, further limiting buying interest in imported ore. On the weather front, major nickel-producing regions in the Philippines continue to be affected by the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) and seasonal rainfall. Parts of Palawan, Visayas, and Mindanao have continued to experience rainfall and thunderstorms. Zambales has been more noticeably affected by the rainy season, with mining operations, inland transportation, and port loading disrupted at some mines, reducing actual shipment capacity. In comparison, areas such as Palawan have maintained a certain level of shipments. As a result, overall Philippine supply has not yet faced a widespread shortage, although regional supply divergence has become more pronounced. From a supply-demand and market sentiment perspective, reduced supply from Zambales has so far failed to provide meaningful price support. The main reasons remain ample downstream inventories in China and weak demand for imported ore. Meanwhile, continued declines in Indonesian nickel ore prices have further weakened the competitiveness of Philippine ore in the Indonesian market. With Indonesia’s second-half October HPM officially lowered, the regional pricing center has moved further downward. If Indonesian domestic ore prices remain under pressure, Philippine miners may need to further adjust FOB quotations to maintain transaction volumes. In the short term, the Philippine nickel ore market is expected to remain weak. Key factors to monitor include the recovery of shipments from Zambales, actual shipment volumes from Palawan, freight rates to China, and movements in Indonesian nickel ore prices. Indonesia: Nickel Ore Prices Accelerate Downward as Second-Half October HPM Is Cut Across the Board On the pricing front, Indonesian nickel ore spot prices continued to weaken this week. According to the latest SMM data, average prices for Ni 1.2% Limonite, Ni 1.3% Saprolite, Ni 1.4% Saprolite, Ni 1.5% Saprolite, and Ni 1.6% Saprolite were US$25.5, US$27.5, US$47.1, US$52.5, and US$57.1/wmt, respectively. Compared with the previous levels of US$26.5, US$28.5, US$51.8, US$58.5, and US$63.4/wmt, prices fell by US$1.0, US$1.0, US$4.7, US$6.0, and US$6.3/wmt, respectively. The steeper declines in medium- to high-grade saprolite indicate that the market’s pricing center has shifted further downward. On the policy pricing front, Indonesia’s Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) has officially published the nickel ore benchmark prices for the second half of October 2026. The nickel HMA for the second half of October was set at US$15,847.67/t, down US$475/t, or 2.91%, from US$16,322.67/t in the first half of October. Corresponding HPM prices were also lowered. Ni 1.2% was set at US$22.44/wmt, down US$0.75/wmt; Ni 1.3% at US$44.58/wmt, down US$1.49/wmt; Ni 1.4% at US$50.05/wmt, down US$1.61/wmt; Ni 1.5% at US$54.48/wmt, down US$1.74/wmt; and Ni 1.6% at US$59.12/wmt, down US$1.88/wmt. The renewed decline in both HMA and HPM has provided miners with a lower pricing benchmark and further reinforced bearish market expectations. On the supply side, supplementary 2026 RKAB quotas are being released gradually, and market attention has shifted from quota approval itself to whether additional quotas can actually be converted into higher production and shipments. New RKAB approvals will not immediately translate into spot supply, as mines still need to arrange equipment deployment, road maintenance, stockpile preparation, and logistics. However, as mines receiving additional quotas gradually resume or expand production, actual nickel ore supply could increase further during the fourth quarter. Against the backdrop of weak demand, expectations of additional supply continue to weigh on ore prices. On the demand side, raw material inventories at Indonesian smelters remain relatively sufficient and are estimated to cover around two months of consumption. As a result, there is limited incentive for aggressive near-term restocking, and spot purchases are mainly focused on meeting essential production requirements. At the same time, the current price correction is showing clear differentiation by ore grade. Prices for Ni 1.4–1.6% saprolite have fallen much more sharply than those for low-grade limonite, suggesting that the previously relatively tight high-grade ore market structure is changing and that bargaining power is shifting further toward buyers. Regarding El Niño and water availability, Indonesia is currently facing persistent dry conditions and shortages of industrial water rather than the heavy rainfall experienced in the Philippines. Industrial water constraints in nickel-processing hubs such as Morowali have already affected operations at some smelting facilities. According to SMM surveys, the operating rates of some RKEF production lines have fallen to around 30–40% of normal levels since September 22. However, the impact currently remains limited to certain production lines and does not represent a broad reduction across the entire industrial park. The main impact of water shortages on the nickel ore market is on the demand side. As RKEF production lines reduce operating rates, their nickel ore consumption declines accordingly, reducing spot purchasing demand from some smelters. Given that raw material inventories are already relatively ample, if water restrictions persist for an extended period, actual ore consumption by smelters could fall further below previous expectations. At present, expectations of increased supply from additional RKAB quotas are coinciding with weaker demand caused by reduced RKEF operating rates, placing pressure on spot ore prices from both sides of the supply-demand balance. From a policy and market sentiment perspective, the 2.91% decline in second-half October HMA, broad-based cuts in HPM across all grades, continued release of additional RKAB quotas, and ample smelter inventories leave little room for a meaningful near-term recovery in ore prices. In particular, the significant decline in Ni 1.4–1.6% saprolite spot prices this week indicates that expectations of lower HPM levels and increased supply are already being reflected in actual market quotations. Meanwhile, low operating rates at some RKEF lines in Morowali are further reducing ore consumption and keeping market sentiment cautious. Looking ahead, the Indonesian nickel ore market is expected to remain weak in the short term. Following the official reduction in the second-half October HPM, market attention will shift to the extent to which the new benchmark prices are transmitted into actual mine transactions and how quickly additional RKAB quotas are converted into real production and shipments. On the demand side, key factors to watch include smelter inventory drawdowns, water availability in Morowali, and operating rates at affected RKEF lines. If mine supply continues to increase while smelter purchasing demand remains constrained by high inventories and water shortages, spot nickel ore prices could face further downside pressure.Oct 19, 2026 10:31 (GMT+8)

news.title: [SMM Analysis] Multiple Headwinds Hit Tungsten Prices, Yet Medium and Long-Term Outlook Remains IntactSMM, October 15: Since July, China's tungsten market has consolidated in a narrow range, with shrinking transaction volumes and downstream demand in the seasonal off-season. Market activity has been largely guided by long-term contract transactions. Entering September, the market expected downstream demand from sectors such as cemented carbide to improve. In early September, upstream tungsten raw material enterprises held firm on quotes, market confidence was moderate, and industry long-term contract prices remained firm overall. However, demand was slow to materialize, and market demand performance was mediocre. Some enterprises had a large backlog of long-term contract deliveries from earlier periods, reducing procurement volumes, and market transactions showed no improvement. APT enterprises were the first to initiate production cuts and destocking. Some enterprises faced cash flow difficulties and sold at discounts to secure liquidity. Before the National Day holiday, downstream stockpiling enthusiasm in China was lackluster, and market transactions hit a freezing point. Mining and smelting enterprises moved to mitigate risk by increasing shipments, resulting in panic selling in the market, with transaction prices trending downward. On the last trading day of September, SMM 65% wolframite concentrates closed at 377,000 yuan/standard tonne, down 39,500 yuan/standard tonne from the beginning of September. SMM APT closed at 550,000 yuan/mt, down 46,500 yuan/mt from early September, with spot orders in the market mainly executed at discounts to list prices. After returning from the National Day holiday, a major Chinese enterprise released long-term contract prices, but industry long-term contract procurement volumes shrank sharply. Market supply liquidity surged dramatically. Smelters, with inventory at high levels from earlier periods and fixed order volumes dropping sharply, faced a full-scale panic sell-off across the market, accelerating the decline across the entire tungsten industry chain. As of October 15, the SMM guidance price for 65% wolframite concentrates closed at 302,000 yuan/standard tonne, down 75,000 yuan/standard tonne within the month and down 71.3% from the mid-March high. APT prices closed at 470,000 yuan/mt, down 80,000 yuan/mt within the month and down 69% from the mid-March high, erasing all gains for the year. The major bearish factors facing the tungsten market in October are as follows: Supply side: Tungsten ore imports surged, breaking the narrative of tight domestic quota balance In 2026, China's total tungsten concentrate mining quota remains tightened, and domestic primary tungsten ore production is mainly down YoY. According to SMM sample data calculations, China's total tungsten concentrate production in the first three quarters of 2026 fell 7.84% YoY. With tightened quota controls and ore grades declining year by year, domestic tungsten concentrate supply is unlikely to see growth in the short term. Due to safety inspections in Luanchuan and other reasons, some tungsten-molybdenum mines have been shut down for extended periods, and the timeline for new projects to reach production has lengthened. China's total tungsten concentrate supply for 2026 is expected to reach 101,000 standard tonnes, down 6.1% YoY. However, domestic mining trading enterprises have stepped up efforts to source and purchase ore overseas. From January to August, China's tungsten concentrate imports surged sharply. According to customs data, China's total tungsten product imports from January to August 2026 amounted to approximately 25,000 mt, up 116% YoY. Based on SMM calculations using actual grades of tungsten concentrate imports from various countries, China's cumulative tungsten concentrate imports in 2026 totaled approximately 17,400 standard tonnes, up 118% YoY. SMM expects China's total tungsten concentrate imports for 2026 to reach 37,000 mt, up 80% YoY, equivalent to approximately 27,000 standard tonnes, an increase of 13,000 standard tonnes YoY, effectively offsetting the decline in domestic tungsten concentrate production. Smelting: Smelters hold high inventory, and increased working capital needs have led to heavier selling pressure in the market Since Q2, although production operating rates in the APT industry have declined, procurement volumes from downstream cemented carbide enterprises have fallen. End-users in the industry mainly consumed previous inventory in H1, and concentrated industry restocking has been slow. Inventory of mainstream smelting products such as APT has accumulated severely. According to incomplete SMM statistics, APT producer inventory in China was nearly 4,000 mt at end-September. In October, mainstream industry players reduced long-term contract procurement volumes to further release liquidity. APT shipments were blocked, corporate cash collection fell short of expectations, and working capital pressure rose significantly. To accelerate payments and reduce inventory depreciation risk, some smelters proactively cut prices to sell and cash out, markedly intensifying selling pressure in the spot market and further driving down the price negotiation center for APT and upstream tungsten concentrates. Demand: Weak consumption in traditional application fields; export market unlikely to see growth Against the backdrop of tungsten prices consolidating at highs in H1 2026, the trend of reduced alloying and material substitution in the cemented carbide industry has become increasingly evident—downstream tool and mold enterprises are widely adopting tungsten-reduced formulations, while ceramic tools and coated hard materials are accelerating the replacement of low and mid-end tungsten-based alloys. Coupled with sluggish manufacturing recovery, operating rates at traditional cemented carbide enterprises remain low and willingness to restock raw materials is subdued. In 2026, tungsten consumption growth in AI/PCB applications has accelerated, but total tungsten usage still accounts for a relatively small share of overall downstream tungsten consumption. Based on SMM estimates from production data of major domestic PCB micro-drill and tungsten hexafluoride producers, total tungsten consumption in the PCB micro-drill and tungsten hexafluoride segments in 2026 is approximately 3,800 mt in metal content, up about 30% YoY, accounting for only about 4.6% of China's total tungsten consumption. Traditional cutting tools, mining, and machining segments remain the main consumers, but performance is weak. Export market: High overseas premiums under controls are unlikely to boost exports of tungsten intermediate products and finished goods Since June 2026, the Ministry of Commerce has intensively introduced dual-use item control policies: adding 10 US military-industrial and rare earth enterprises to the embargo list; improving reporting mechanisms for violations involving strategic minerals such as tungsten, molybdenum, and rare earths; adding 40 Japanese military-related entities in two tiers, subject to comprehensive embargoes and strict case-by-case approvals; and working with customs to tighten clearance verification for precision machine tools, comprehensively strengthening export controls on strategic minerals and military-industrial equipment. Exports of dual-use tungsten intermediate products are unlikely to see growth. In January-August, China's total exports of tungsten intermediate products were approximately 9,071 mt, down about 15% YoY cumulatively. Domestic cemented carbide blade products have had a price advantage over overseas products since H2 this year, but exports have still not shown growth expectations. In January-August, China's total exports of cemented carbide blades were 1,967 mt, down 15% YoY, which may be related to weak operating rates in overseas end-user manufacturing and trade volume fluctuations caused by tariff volatility. Overall, the rapid decline in tungsten prices this round was essentially the result of the bursting of the previous price bubble combined with a synchronized inventory cycle, as market sentiment quickly shifted from holding back supply in anticipation of higher prices to prioritizing cash. The sustained price drop triggered panic selling across the industry chain, with ore traders, smelters, and some cemented carbide supporting enterprises selling ahead of schedule to reduce risk, further amplifying the negative feedback loop. Downstream cemented carbide enterprises maintained only just-in-time procurement, no longer making precautionary restocking, with orders placed on an as-needed basis. Long-term contract negotiations dragged on with wide pricing disagreements, and while spot cargo supply increased, effective transactions remained sluggish, with most deals involving passive selling at concessions. In the short term, the market is in a phase of inventory destocking and sentiment repair, and the tungsten market in October is likely to be dominated by an accelerated bottoming-out trend. For prices to stop falling, the industry chain needs to show the following signals: first, a broader expansion of voluntary production cuts in APT and tungsten concentrates, with deep losses at the smelting stage triggering spontaneous output reductions to ease spot selling pressure; second, marginal improvement in downstream cemented carbide orders, with the traditional manufacturing mini-peak season in Q4 driving a recovery in orders for cutting tools and mining tools, as well as low-price-driven restocking at lower levels; third, a slowdown in the arrival pace of imported tungsten ore, as price inversion in China suppresses purchases of overseas ore and weakens the impact of import growth; and fourth, a contraction in recycled tungsten supply, as low prices reduce recycling incentives and lessen the substitution of recycled materials for primary tungsten. On the export front, Chinese tungsten products now have a price advantage, and overseas pre-Christmas stockpiling presents potential growth. However, approval restrictions on dual-use items remain in place, and only non-controlled categories such as ordinary cemented carbide inserts and tungsten powder are expected to see modest volume increases, which are unlikely to dominate the market trend. From a medium and long-term perspective, China's policy of controlling total tungsten concentrate mining volume remains unchanged, primary ore production continues to decline, and supply rigidity persists due to falling ore grades and long commissioning cycles for new projects. Tungsten's strategic resource attributes remain intact, and supply is expected to stay in contraction through 2027. Emerging demand from downstream PCB micro-drills, tungsten hexafluoride, and PV tungsten wire continues to grow, but the volume is not yet enough to offset weakness in traditional cemented carbide consumption.
